meta: Dramas like If You Wish Upon Me: hospice dramas, found family, and Korean dramas about being unwanted.
standfirst: A hospice, a wish-granting team, and Ji Chang Wook playing a man nobody has ever wanted: an ex-convict orphan with an eating disorder and a temper he cannot hold. It is the best work he has done, quiet and damaged and never played for charm. The draw is the tonal range, because comedy, sweetness and real cruelty share the same hour. Know before you start that self-harm and suicide attempts are in it, handled with care but present. The second half is weaker than the first and the romance is an afterthought. The final stretch is devastating because fourteen hours taught you to love somebody the world did not.

picks.why: The unfinished business of the dead, and a guardian nobody expected to be good at it. Same structure of a team entering the worst room in somebody's life and treating it with proper attention, same central bond between a damaged man and a young person he did not ask for. Difference: eight episodes, no romance, heavy 5, and it is colder in the best possible way.

Damaged people, care work, and love as an act of maintenance. Same subject of somebody unloved from childhood learning to be around others, and the same hospital-adjacent setting that gives the show a rotating cast of patients. Difference: it is stylised and romance-led, and the fairy-tale framing does a lot of the emotional lifting.

A ward, a patient per episode, and kindness with procedure attached. Same insistence that the people in the beds are the point and the staff are colleagues rather than saints. Difference: no wish, no found family, no supernatural sweetness, and the pastel packaging hides something considerably heavier.

Dignity at the end of a life, treated as an achievable thing. Same central pairing of an older person with limited time and a young man with no direction, and the same refusal to make either of them a lesson. Difference: no illness plot and no ensemble, twelve gentle episodes with nothing cruel in them.

Found family assembled out of broken homes. Same belief that the people who choose you outrank the ones who did not, and the same warmth toward adults doing a bad job kindly. Difference: the childhood half is the good half and the adult half turns into a love triangle, so it does not finish what it starts.

Sung Dong Il again, and mental illness written with warmth rather than pity. Same house of people looking after each other badly and then better, same mix of jokes and real damage. Difference: it is a romance first, glossier, and its central reveal is structural rather than emotional.

against.title: Hi Bye, Mama!
against.why: The tearjerker handed to everybody, and it works by schedule. Forty-nine days, a deadline and a family, with each beat aimed squarely at your tear ducts. This show earns the last stretch across fourteen hours instead, and the difference in method matters.

against.title: Hospital Playlist
against.why: Paired for the medical setting and the warmth, and it is a hangout show. Five friends, a band and patients who resolve. There is no hospice weight in it, and no character anywhere near as unwanted as the lead here.

against.title: Uncontrollably Fond
against.why: Recommended because of the terminal diagnosis, and it uses it as leverage. A star, a secret illness and a melodrama that reaches for the disease whenever the plot stalls. If You Wish Upon Me is about care work, not about dying beautifully.
